thesis.claim: The door that closed on hand-written raiders in B2's late worlds, and the crews' failure there, come from B2's own rules. In B1's two long worlds, which keep no share of an agent's tokens at home, count a holder's own stake once, let a child start with a single token and have no old age, patches of 5% planted at iterations 2,000, 5,000 and 10,000, with the raiders' rules reading each world's own, take hold, counted by the tokens they hold, in at least 5 of the 18 plantings of lone raiders, and in at least as many plantings of crews as of lone raiders.
thesis.why: In B2's worlds at 5,000 and 10,000 no lone raider and no crew took hold in 30 plantings each (Chapters 97 and 102), for reasons that are B2's rules: a late patch held two tokens an agent and seven in ten of its agents a single token, which B2's home share keeps from being staked; a holder's own stake counts one and a half times, so a raider needs three tokens to take one, and a crew's stake that finds no partner is lost; and a patch that cannot breed dies with its founders at age 100. B1 has none of these rules, and its worlds stay rich: the median agent holds 4 to 15 tokens at these eras. Reading B1's rules, a raider stakes everything it holds, so a raid moves it onto the node it takes, and it needs only more than the neighbour holds. A child can be a single token in B1, so a patch is counted by the tokens it holds rather than by its agents; counted so, B2's verdicts are the same (lone raiders 4, 0 and 0 of 15; crews none). The breeding raider and the breeding turtle of Chapter 103 are planted too, and reported.
thesis.confirm: Counted by tokens (alive after 300 iterations, more tokens than the patch began with, and more than the control planted in the same place), lone raiders take hold in at least 5 of the 18 plantings, and crews in at least as many as lone raiders.
thesis.refute: Lone raiders take hold in 4 or fewer of the 18, or crews in fewer than lone raiders: that verdict of B2 holds in B1 too, and the chapter says which.
